step_1_vocabulary_search.action: grep -rn 'disposition' and 'view_tag'/'viewTag' across the ENTIRE exported evidence tree (data/**, docs/math-foundations.md)
step_1_vocabulary_search.result: 0 hits, in any file, in any casing variant
step_1_vocabulary_search.consequence: no cached wiki text and no formula in docs/math-foundations.md defines a `disposition` or a `view_tag`, so no entry of this map is derivable from the oracle evidence tree. The map cannot be recomputed entry-by-entry from game data — there is no game data behind it.

step_2_cardinality_falsification_attempt.action: test whether 178 corresponds to any catalog in the cache, which would make the key space checkable
step_2_cardinality_falsification_attempt.result: 178 matches NO catalog in the cache and no sum of catalogs that has a domain meaning
step_2_cardinality_falsification_attempt.consequence: the key space is not a data catalog (champions/items/runes/atoms). It is consistent with a per-scenario key space (one entry per rendered combat row / event across the coupled participants of this one scenario), which the oracle evidence tree does not contain. Cardinality therefore neither confirms nor falsifies the leaf. Note this DOES rule out one failure mode: the map is not a mis-sized copy of the champion list (173) or the item list (324/288).

step_3_contract_consistency.action: check whether a per-row {label, view} pair is the documented intent of the P4 workstream, using only cached worklist text and the math doc
step_3_contract_consistency.finding: yes — the P4 trust-label contract quoted in data/worklists/p5-ux-task.md specifies exactly a per-row certainty label plus the view that renders it, and docs/math-foundations.md is built on the same 'every family is labeled' principle (EXACT / APPROX verdicts in the Section 5 audit table). A dispositions map alongside the combat payload is the shape those sources describe.
step_3_contract_consistency.consequence: the new leaf is consistent with the documented contract; the old absent state simply predates the feature and asserts nothing.

step_4_contradiction_check.action: look for any cached source that assigns this leaf a different value, or any numeric claim inside the map that could disagree with the wiki cache
step_4_contradiction_check.result: none. The leaf holds only labels and view tags; no cached source assigns it any value at all, and no number in it can conflict with data/champions.json, data/items.json or data/runes.json.
step_4_contradiction_check.consequence: there is no evidence of error in the new value, and none in favour of the absent state.

what_was_verified: no cached source (wiki text, item/champion/rune cache, math doc) assigns this leaf any value, so nothing in the evidence tree contradicts the new value
the leaf carries no game-derived quantity, so no wiki number can be violated by it
the {disposition, view_tag} shape matches the P4 trust-label contract documented in the cached worklist
178 is not a mis-sized stand-in for the champion catalogue (173), the item catalogue (324), the SR-available item set (288) or the mid BIS candidate set (96)
what_could_NOT_be_verified: the individual 178 entries — which key gets which disposition, and which view_tag each carries. These have no referent in cached game data; they can only be checked against the engine's own labeling rules, which live in src/ and are out of bounds for this runbook.
the exact cardinality 178: the key space appears to be per-scenario combat rows, which the evidence tree does not contain.
verification_scope_and_limits.verdict_basis: The oracle's job is to catch a game-data-wrong value. This leaf makes no game-data claim; the evidence tree contradicts nothing in it, and the old state (absence) is not a competing correct value — it is the pre-feature state. The verdict is therefore 'new_value_correct' in the sense of 'no error detectable and consistent with the documented contract', NOT an entry-level certification of all 178 labels.

recommendation_for_the_gate: Because this leaf is non-numeric and per-scenario, the golden gate cannot oracle it against the cache. If entry-level assurance is wanted, it should come from a unit test over the labeling rule (every rendered combat row gets exactly one disposition, drawn from the closed P4 vocabulary, with a view_tag naming a declared view), not from the golden snapshot.
